assessment.summary: A compatibility organization hierarchy reduces scope-model drift while preserving tenant isolation and rollback.

nonNegotiables: Organization ancestry is loaded by the server from the database.
Only explicit global hierarchy grants can cross a security tenant.
Existing flat scope columns remain available during migration.
assumptions: No measured latency or memory budget was supplied.

opportunities.title: Centralize hierarchical scope containment
opportunities.summary: Represent organization ancestry once and attach a trusted path to resource authorization facts.
opportunities.diagnosis: Flat resource scope fields and exact matching require engine changes for every new organization level and cannot safely express controlled cross-tenant governance.

evidence.claim: ResourceScope represented each level as a separate optional ID.
Authorization used hard tenant equality and exact per-kind matching.
Distributor, brand and store kinds were reserved while delegation remained flat.
The existing server-owned resource scope boundary can safely carry database-derived ancestry.

desiredInvariants: Every hierarchical match is supported by a database-derived ancestor path.
Only platform and distributor grants can authorize resources in another security tenant.
Role permission edits invalidate every active membership that holds the role.

options.title: Continue expanding flat scope fields
options.summary: Add distributor and future IDs to every contract, row projection and matcher.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Additional cases can serve current levels but preserve structural drift.

tradeoffs.assessment: Explicit cases can stay fail closed, but future omissions remain likely.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Add cross-tenant tests for every scope kind.

tradeoffs.assessment: Exact comparisons add no database hop.
Only bounded optional IDs are added.
More duplicated projections create compatibility drift.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run contract parity tests across every route.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new table appears, but every level requires coordinated releases.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Track files changed for the next scope addition.

tradeoffs.assessment: This is the smallest immediate patch.

residualRisks: Scope semantics remain distributed across contracts, SQL projections and matchers.

workPackages: Add flat scope fields and tests.
acceptanceCriteria: Every new level has an explicit matcher.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert the new fields and matchers.

options.title: Add a compatibility organization hierarchy
options.summary: Add organization nodes and a closure table while keeping legacy resource columns.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Ancestor containment becomes data-driven; cross-tenant guard tests remain required.
Role-permission invalidation is added while global grant ceremony remains deferred.

tradeoffs.assessment: Ancestry comes from one server-owned database boundary and lower scopes cannot cross tenants.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run cross-tenant and malformed-path tests plus SQL assertions.

tradeoffs.assessment: Resource scope RPCs add an indexed closure lookup.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare p95 scope lookup latency before production enablement.

tradeoffs.assessment: Closure rows grow with the number of ancestor-descendant pairs.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure closure row count and index size on a production-shaped fixture.

tradeoffs.assessment: Legacy flat fields remain a rollback path; hierarchy mutation needs controlled transactions.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test node moves, cycles and rollback to flat-only reads.

tradeoffs.assessment: Operators must monitor hierarchy consistency and closure rebuilds.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Add mapping and closure integrity checks to deployment verification.

tradeoffs.assessment: Backfill is additive and does not remove existing fields or APIs.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Execute all migrations against an empty PostgreSQL 17 database and a production-shaped snapshot.

residualRisks: Global grant lifecycle is not yet exposed.
Large hierarchy move performance is unmeasured.

acceptanceCriteria: Role permission edits bump affected memberships.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Stop returning org_unit_path; the flat matcher remains available.

options.title: Replace legacy scope columns immediately
options.summary: Move all reads and writes to organization IDs in one release.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Flat fields disappear but every current query and write path must migrate atomically.

tradeoffs.assessment: One model reduces ambiguity after a complete cutover.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Audit every resource lookup and mutation after conversion.

tradeoffs.assessment: All query plans change and no production-shaped benchmark exists.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark complete catalog, order and admin workloads.

tradeoffs.assessment: Closure indexes replace some denormalized fields but actual size is unknown.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare database and application memory on a restored snapshot.

tradeoffs.assessment: A broad atomic cutover removes the tested rollback path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a full restore and rollback rehearsal.

tradeoffs.assessment: Deployment coordinates every service and database caller.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inventory and stage all callers before cutover.

tradeoffs.assessment: Historical data and every RPC require conversion at once.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Dry-run against a production copy and reconcile every row.

residualRisks: Unknown callers can fail after the irreversible cutover.

affectedComponents: all database and application scope callers
workPackages: Replace every scope field and query.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Restore the database and prior application release.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the additive compatibility hierarchy under the current uptime and rollback constraints.

openQuestions: Which identities may receive a platform or distributor scope?
What production-shaped upper bound should closure rebuild time satisfy?
